images.title: FEEL Boutique Plaza
images.description:
FEEL was conceived as a third place for the Omani community, bridging the distance between work and home and creating a setting centred on connection and shared experience. Every element was developed from this central idea. Although the café, retail, gallery, library and wellness spaces retain individual identities, their materials, furniture and architectural language form a continuous environment.

The furniture was designed through research into the habits and preferences of Muscat’s residents, with social interaction placed at the centre of the hospitality experience. Locally rooted tiles reinterpret traditional cultural motifs: a single modular tile can be arranged in multiple configurations to form changing carpet-like patterns. Half arches derived from traditional Arabic architecture remain intentionally incomplete, becoming full arches only where an important view is framed.

A verse by Hafez was integrated into the window coverings and spatial dividers, extending the project’s conceptual language into typography and poetry. The result is an adaptive reuse project in which contemporary hospitality, Omani memory and communal life are brought together within the fabric of an existing house.

Project: FEEL Boutique Plaza
Architecture firm: Innovative Corner Design (ICD.co.)
Principal architect and interior design: Jalal Mashhadi Fard

images.title: LOOKOUT/IN Café
images.description:
LOOK IN invites visitors to observe themselves while creating the possibility of an encounter with someone else. The project develops a continuous exchange between seeing and being seen, between the mystery concealed within a reflection and the gaze attempting to understand it.

In the main café space, mirrors positioned vertically along both sides of the corridor produce a layered and visually expanded interior. Their role extends beyond making the room appear larger. They create an uncertain boundary between physical space and reflection: the corridor seems to continue beyond its actual limit, yet as the visitor approaches, their own reflected body becomes a barrier to the imagined space behind the mirror.

The social table translates Matthew Carmona’s Triangle Principle into furniture and spatial organisation. Two people occupy the edges of an implied triangle while a tree forms its third point, gently defining territory while supporting interaction. The arrangement increases the possibility of eye contact, and the alignment of the mirrors causes different gazes to converge across the room.

Project: Look in/out

images.title: Jan Plaza
images.description:
The architecture of Jan is a poetic reflection on love and light. The proportions of its façade draw from the Tabatabaei and Borujerdi houses of Kashan, historic residences whose architecture carries an enduring narrative of love. In Jan, the building comes alive through changing daylight and returns that radiance to the city after dark.

The interior is structured through a personal reading of Rumi’s philosophy. Three axes organise the narrative: the Y axis represents the mind of the lover, the X axis marks the presence of the beloved within that mind, and the Z axis is light itself, understood as the force of love. Public spaces unfold along the lover’s mind, reception halls embody the beloved, and illumination binds the composition vertically.

On the central axis, the principal mirrored arch becomes a mihrab for the lover. Repeated nested arches keep the beloved present from multiple viewpoints, while paired half arches in the reception spaces evoke an embrace. Verses by Rumi, composed in architectural Kufic script, operate as narrators throughout the building.

The plan also balances complementary forms of energy. Waiting areas and women’s spaces occupy the right side as the receptive and contemplative Yin, while management, service and men’s spaces occupy the left as the active and ordered Yang. Vertical proportions draw the gaze upward, suggesting that the final meaning of love lies beyond the material world.

The site was formerly a mulberry orchard. Its remembered sweetness becomes part of the project’s imagery: Jan rises as a white blossom from dark earth, transforming the memory held within the ground into light. Its emblem develops from the Shamseh Chalipa, beginning with the point or pixel as the smallest unit and expanding toward an infinite field, a metaphor for the lover moving beyond the limits of the self.

images.title: Keluchick Handmade Chocolate House
images.description:
Keluchick Handmade Chocolate House begins with the idea that chocolate evokes more than taste. It can recall childhood, awaken imagination and offer a brief departure from the intensity of everyday life. The project translates these emotional qualities into an architectural experience.

Set within a dense urban context, the store is organised as a gradual sequence rather than an immediate retail display. The fragmented entrance geometry creates a measured transition from the city into the interior. Water forms an essential part of this threshold, using reflection, movement and sound to slow the visitor’s arrival and establish a different atmosphere.

The main space is shaped by reflection, suspension and perceptual ambiguity. Reflective stainless steel produces layered visual relationships and softens the boundary between physical space and its mirrored image. Suspended display elements introduce lightness and create a sense of separation from the outside world.

Oblique lines generate triangular spaces for pausing, conversation and interaction. These social conditions emerge from the geometry itself rather than being added as separate zones. The chocolate making process remains visible, placing craftsmanship in direct dialogue with visitors and transforming chocolate from a product into an experience.

Project: Keluchick Handmade Chocolate House

images.title: New Generation
images.description:
New Generation is a residential project currently in development on Abuzar Boulevard in Mashhad, within the established Ahmadabad neighbourhood. It is being designed for a new generation of residents whose understanding of luxury is shaped less by size and formality, and more by adaptability, spatial quality and everyday experience.

The project moves from fixed domestic conventions toward a more flexible way of living: smaller but smarter apartments, open social kitchens, adaptable living areas, home offices, walk-in closets and private master suites. Its architecture negotiates openness and privacy through layered façades, planted thresholds and adjustable screens.

The main elevation combines transparent living spaces with recessed private bedroom suites. A protective outer layer of perforated modules filters daylight, air and views; selected modules operate as mirrors, open apertures or integrated lights, allowing the façade to shift between privacy, reflection and illumination.

Project: New Generation Apartment
Architect: Jalal Mashhadi Fard
Client: Mr. Zarandi and Level Construction Group
Location: Abuzar Boulevard, Ahmadabad, Mashhad, Iran
Status: In Progress

images.title: Homay Wellness Center
images.description:
Homay Wellness Center is conceived as a landmark destination where sport, health, hospitality and landscape form one continuous experience. Set within a mountainous terrain, the proposal follows the contours of the site through a family of curved volumes, planted roofs and a multi-level movement loop.

The programme brings together a professional gym, indoor and outdoor pools, a luxury restaurant and VIP club, a hotel and café, and a medical health centre. Rather than separating these functions into isolated buildings, the architecture links them through terraces, bridges and walking routes, allowing movement, views and landscape to become the connective tissue of the project.

A flowing timber screen wraps the glazed volumes, filtering sun and views while giving the complex a unified identity. The buildings step with the slope, preserving panoramic views and creating a sequence of interior and exterior spaces for exercise, recovery, dining and rest.

Project: Homay Wellness Center
Architect: Jalal Mashhadi Fard Studio
Client: Mr. Ali Tabrizi
Status: Design Stage · Unbuilt

images.title: ToBe
images.description:
ToBe is a social café conceived around the tension between being and not being—and the shared space in which we become. The identity begins with two dark circular forms and a warm illuminated centre: me, you and the collective we. This elemental diagram is translated into an interior organised around encounter, reflection and changing atmosphere.

A long communal table becomes the project’s social spine. Warm backlit planes meet cool blue reflections, while brushed stainless steel, mirrored surfaces, smoked translucent seating and glass blocks multiply people, light and movement. The space shifts character from morning to night without losing its restrained material language.

Creative direction, identity and spatial concept are developed as one continuous system. Graphic elements, lighting, material palette and architecture all express the same proposition: between being and not being, we become.

Project: ToBe Social Café
Architecture and creative direction: Jalal Mashhadi Fard
Status: Concept Design
